1.1: The wordes of Amos, who was among the heardmen at Tecoa, which he saw upon Israel, in the dayes of Uzziah king of Judah, and in the dayes of Jeroboam the sonne of Joash King of Israel, two yeere before the earthquake.
1.2: And he said, The Lord shall roar from Zion, and utter his voyce from Jerusalem, and the dwelling places of the shepheards shall perish, and the top of Carmel shall wither,
1.3: Thus saith the Lord, For three transgressions of Damascus, and for four I will not turn to it, because they have threshed Gilead with threshing instruments of yron.
1.4: Therefore will I send a fire into the house of Hazael, and it shall deuoure the palaces of Ben-hadad.
1.5: I will break also the barres of Damascus, and cut off the inhabitant of Bikeath-aven: and him that holdeth the scepter out of Beth-eden, and the people of Aram shall goe into captiuitie unto Kir, sayth the Lord.
1.6: Thus sayth the Lord, For three transgressions of Azzah, and for four, I will not turn to it, because they caried away prisoners the whole captiuitie to shut them up in Edom.
1.7: Therefore will I send a fire upon the walles of Azzah, and it shall deuoure the palaces thereof.
1.8: And I will cut off the inhabitant from Ashdod, and him that holdeth the scepter from Ashkelon, and turn mine hand to Ekron, and the remnant of the Philistims shall perish, sayth the Lord God.
1.9: Thus sayth the Lord, For three transgressions of Tyrus, and for four, I will not turn to it, because they shut the whole captiuitie in Edom, and have not remembred the brotherly covenant.
1.10: Therefore wil I send a fire upon ye walles of Tyrus, and it shall deuoure the palaces thereof.
1.11: Thus sayeth the Lord, For three transgressions of Edom, and for four, I will not turn to it, because hee did pursue his brother with the sword, and did cast off all pitie, and his anger spoyled him evermore, and his wrath watched him alway.
1.12: Therefore will I send a fire upon Teman, and it shall deuoure the palaces of Bozrah.
1.13: Thus sayth ye Lord, For three transgressions of the children of Ammon, and for four, I will not turn to it, because they have ript up the women with child of Gilead, that they might enlarge their border.
1.14: Therefore will I kindle a fire in the wall of Rabbah, and it shall deuoure the palaces thereof, with shouting in the day of battell, and with a tempest in the day of the whirlewinde.
1.15: And their King shall go into captiuitie, he and his princes together, saith the Lord.

2.1: Thus sayth the Lord, For three transgressions of Moab, and for four, I will not turn to it, because it burnt the bones of the King of Edom into lime.
2.2: Therefore will I send a fire upon Moab, and it shall deuoure the palaces of Kerioth, and Moab shall die with tumult, with shouting, and with the sound of a trumpet.
2.3: And I will cut off the judge out of the mids thereof, and will slay all the princes thereof with him, sayth the Lord.
2.4: Thus saith the Lord, For three transgressions of Judah, and for four, I will not turn to it, because they have cast away the Law of the Lord, and have not kept his commandementes, and their lies caused them to ere after the which their fathers have walked.
2.5: Therefore will I send a fire upon Judah, and it shall deuoure the palaces of Jerusalem.
2.6: Thus sayth the Lord, For three transgressions of Israel, and for four, I will not turn to it, because they sold the righteous for silver and the poor for shooes.
2.7: They gap over the head of the poor, in the dust of the earth, and pervert the wayes of the meek: and a man and his father will goe in to a mayde to dishonour mine holy Name.
2.8: And they lye down upon clothes layde to pledge by every altar: and they drink the wine of the condemned in the house of their God.
2.9: Yet destroyed I the Amorite before the, whose height was like the height of the cedars, and he was strong as the okes: notwithstanding I destroyed his fruit from above, and his root from beneath.
2.10: Also I brought you up from the land of Egypt, and led you fourtie yeres thorowe the wilderness, to possess the land of the Amorite.
2.11: And I raysed up of your sonnes for Prophets, and of your yong men for Nazarites. Is it not even thus, O ye children of Israel, sayth the Lord?
2.12: But ye gave the Nazarites wine to drink, and commanded the Prophetes, saying, Prophecie not.
2.13: Behold, I am pressed under you as a cart is pressed that is full of sheaves.
2.14: Therefore the flight shall perish from the swift, and the strong shall not strengthen his force, neither shall the mightie save his life.
2.15: Nor he that handleth the bow, shall stand, and he that is swift of foot, shall not escape, neyther shall he that rideth the horse, save his life.
2.16: And he that is of a mighty courage among the strong men, shall flee away naked in that day, sayth the Lord.

3.1: Hear this word that the Lord pronounceth against you, O children of Israel, even against the whole familie which I brought up from the land of Egypt, saying,
3.2: You onely have I knowen of all the families of the earth: therefore I will visit you for all your iniquities.
3.3: Can two walk together except they bee agreed?
3.4: Will a lion roar in ye forest, when he hath no pray? or wil a lions whelp cry out of his den, if he have taken nothing?
3.5: Can a bird fall in a snare upon the earth, where no fouler is? or will he take up the snare from the earth, and have taken nothing at all?
3.6: Or shall a trumpet be blowen in the citie, and the people be not afraid? or shall there be evil in a citie, and the Lord hath not done it?
3.7: Surely the Lord God will doe nothing, but he reueileth his secret unto his seruantes the Prophets.
3.8: The lyon hath roared: who will not bee afraid? the Lord God hath spoken: who can but prophecie?
3.9: Proclayme in the palaces at Ashdod, and in the palaces in the land of Egypt, and say, Assemble your selves upon the mountaines of Samaria: so behold the great tumultes in the middes thereof, and the oppressed in the middes thereof.
3.10: For they know not to doe right, sayth the Lord: they store up violence, and robbery in their palaces.
3.11: Therefore thus saith the Lord God, An adversary shall come even round about the countrey, and shall bring down thy strength from thee, and thy palaces shalbe spoyled.
3.12: Thus saieth the Lord, As the shephearde taketh out of the mouth of the lyon two legges, or a piece of an ear: so shall the children of Israel be taken out that dwell in Samaria in the corner of a bed, and in Damascus, as in a couch.
3.13: Hear, and testifie in the house of Iaakob, saith the Lord God, the God of hostes.
3.14: Surely in the day that I shall visit the transgressions of Israel upon him, I wil also visit the altars of Beth-el, and the hornes of the altar shall be broken off, and fall to the ground.
3.15: And I wil smite the winter house with the sommer house, and the houses of yuorie shall perish, and the great houses shalbe consumed, sayth the Lord.

4.1: Hear this word, ye kine of Bashan that are in the mountain of Samaria, which oppress the poor, and destroy the needie, and they say to their masters, Bring, and let us drink.
4.2: The Lord God hath sworn by his holines, that loe, the dayes shall come upon you, that hee wil take you away with thornes, and your posteritie with fish hookes.
4.3: And ye shall goe out at the breaches every kow forward: and ye shall cast your selves out of the palace, saith the Lord.
4.4: Come to Beth-el, and transgress: to Gilgal, and multiplie transgression, and bring your sacrifices in the morning, and your tithes after three yeres.
4.5: And offer a thankesgiuing of leaven, publish and proclaim the free offrings: for this liketh you, O ye children of Israel, saith the Lord God.
4.6: And therefore have I given you cleannes of teeth in all your cities, and scarceness of bread in all your places, yet have ye not returned unto me, saith the Lord.
4.7: And also I have withholden the rain from you, when there were yet three moneths to the harvest, and I caused it to rain upon one citie, and have not caused it to rain upon another citie: one piece was rained upon, and the piece whereupon it rained not, withered.
4.8: So two or three cities wandred unto one citie to drink water, but they were not satisfied: yet have ye not returned unto me, saith the Lord.
4.9: I have smitten you with blasting, and mildew: your great gardens and your vineyardes, and your figtrees, and your olive trees did the palmer worm deuoure: yet have ye not returned unto me, saith the Lord.
4.10: Pestilence have I sent among you, after the maner of Egypt: your yong men have I slain with the sword, and have taken away your horses: and I have made the stink of your tentes to come up even into your nostrels: yet have yee not returned unto me, saith the Lord.
4.11: I have overthrow you, as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorah: and ye were as a firebrand pluckt out of the burning: yet have ye not returned unto me, saith the Lord.
4.12: Therefore, thus wil I do unto thee, O Israel: and because I wil doe this unto thee, prepare to meet thy God, O Israel.
4.13: For lo, he that formeth the mountaines, and createth the wind, and declareth unto man what is his thought: which maketh the morning darkenesse, and walketh upon the hie places of the earth, the Lord God of hostes is his Name.

5.1: Hear ye this word, which I lift up upon you, even a lamentation of the house of Israel.
5.2: The virgin Israel is fallen, and shall no more rise: she is left upon her land, and there is none to raise her up.
5.3: For thus saith ye Lord God, The citie which went out by a thousand, shall leave an hundreth: and that which went forth by an hundreth, shall leave ten to the house of Israel.
5.4: For thus saith the Lord unto the house of Israel, Seek ye me, and ye shall live.
5.5: But seek not Beth-el, nor enter into Gilgal, and go not to Beer-sheba: for Gilgal shall goe into captiuitie, and Beth-el shall come to nought.
5.6: Seek the Lord, and yee shall live, least he break out like fire in the house of Joseph and deuoure it, and there be none to quench it in Beth-el.
5.7: They turn iudgement to wormewood, and leave off righteousnes in the earth.
5.8: He maketh Pleiades, and Orion, and he turneth the shadow of death into the morning, and he maketh the day dark as night: he calleth the waters of the sea, and powreth them out upon the open earth: the Lord is his Name.
5.9: He strengtheneth the destroyer against the mightie: and the destroyer shall come against the fortress.
5.10: They have hated him, that rebuked in the gate: and they abhorred him that speaketh uprightly.
5.11: Forasmuch then as your treading is upon the poor, and yee take from him burdens of wheat, ye have built houses of hewen stone, but ye shall not dwel in them: ye have plated pleasant vineyards, but ye shall not drink wine of them.
5.12: For I know your manifold transgressions, and your mightie sinnes: they afflict the just, they take rewards, and they oppress the poor in ye gate.
5.13: Therefore the prudent shall keep silence in that time, for it is an evil time.
5.14: Seek good and not evil, that ye may live: and the Lord God of hostes shalbe with you, as you have spoken.
5.15: Hate the evil, and love the good, and establish iudgement in the gate: it may bee that the Lord God of hostes will be merciful unto the remnant of Joseph.
5.16: Therfore the Lord God of hosts, the Lord saith thus, Mourning shalbe in all streetes: and they shall say in al the hie wayes, Alas, alas: and they shall call the husbandman to lamentation, and such as can mourn, to mourning.
5.17: And in al the vines shalbe lamentation: for I wil pass through thee, saith the Lord.
5.18: Woe unto you, that desire the day of the Lord: what have you to do with it? the day of the Lord is darkenes and not light.
5.19: As if a man did flee from a lyon, and a bear met him: or went into the house, and leaned his hand on the wall, and a serpent bit him.
5.20: Shal not the day of the Lord be darkenes, and not light? even darkenes and no light in it?
5.21: I hate and abhorre your feast dayes, and I wil not smell in your solemn assemblies.
5.22: Though ye offer me burnt offrings and meat offrings, I wil not accept them: neither will I regard the peace offrings of your fat beasts.
5.23: Take thou away from me the multitude of thy songs (for I wil not hear the melodie of thy violes)
5.24: And let iudgement runne down as waters, and righteousness as a mightie river.
5.25: Have ye offered unto me sacrifices and offrings in the wilderness fourtie yeeres, O house of Israel?
5.26: But you have borne Siccuth your King, and Chiun your images, and the star of your gods, which ye made to your selves.
5.27: Therefore wil I cause you to goe into captiuitie beyond Damascus, saith the Lord, whose Name is the God of hostes.

6.1: Woe to them that are at ease in Zion and trust in the moutaine of Samaria, which were famous at the beginning of the nations: and the house of Israel came to them.
6.2: Goe you unto Calneh, and see: and from thence goe you to Hamath the great: then goe down to Gath of the Philistims: be they better then these kingdomes? or the border of their land greater then your border,
6.3: Ye that put far away the evil day, and approch to the seat of iniquitie?
6.4: They lie upon beddes of yuorie, and stretch themselves upon their beddes, and eat the lambes of the flock, and the calves out of the stall.
6.5: They sing to the sound of the viol: they invent to themselves instruments of musike like David.
6.6: They drink wine in bowles, and anoynt themselves with the chief ointments, but no man is sory for the affliction of Joseph.
6.7: Therefore now shall they go captive with the first that go captive, and the sorow of them that stretched themselves, is at hand.
6.8: The Lord God hath sworn by himself, saith the Lord God of hostes, I abhorre the excellencie of Iaakob, and hate his palaces: therefore wil I deliver up the citie with all that is therein.
6.9: And if there remain ten men in one house, they shall die.
6.10: And his uncle shall take him up and burn him to cary out the bones out of the house, and shall say unto him, that is by ye sides of the house, Is there yet any with thee? And he shall say, None. Then shall he say, Hold thy tongue: for we may not remember the Name of the Lord.
6.11: For behold, the Lord commandeth, and he will smite the great house with breaches, and the litle house with clefts.
6.12: Shal horses runne upon the rock? or wil one plow there with oxen? for yee have turned iudgement into gall, and the fruit of righteousnes into wormewood.
6.13: Ye reioyce in a thing of nought: yee say, Have not wee gotten us hornes by our own strength?
6.14: But behold, I wil raise up against you a nation, O house of Israel, sayeth the Lord God of hostes: and they shall afflict you, from the entring in of Hamath unto the river of the wildernes.

7.1: Thus hath the Lord God shewed unto mee, and behold, he formed grashoppers in the beginning of ye shooting up of the latter grouth: and loe, it was in the latter grouth after the Kings mowing.
7.2: And when they had made an end of eating the grass of the land, then I said, O Lord God, spare, I beseech thee: who shall raise up Iaakob? for he is small.
7.3: So the Lord repented for this. It shall not be, saith the Lord.
7.4: Thus also hath the Lord God shewed unto me, and behold, the Lord God called to iudgement by fire, and it deuoured the great deep, and did eat up a part.
7.5: Then said I, O Lord God, cease, I beseech thee: who shall raise up Iaakob? for he is small.
7.6: So the Lord repented for this. This also shall not be, saith the Lord God.
7.7: Thus again he shewed me, and behold, the Lord stood upon a wall made by line with a line in his hand.
7.8: And the Lord said unto me, Amos, what seest thou? And I said, A line. Then said the Lord, Behold, I wil set a line in the middes of my people Israel, and wil pass by them no more.
7.9: And the hye places of Izhak shalbe desolate, and the temples of Israel shalbe destroyed: and I wil rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword.
7.10: Then Amaziah the Priest of Beth-el sent to Jeroboam King of Israel, saying, Amos hath conspired against thee in the middes of the house of Israel: the land is not able to bear all his wordes.
7.11: For thus Amos saith, Jeroboam shall die by the sword, and Israel shalbe led away captive out of their own land.
7.12: Also Amaziah sayde unto Amos, O thou the Seer, goe, flee thou away into the land of Judah, and there eat thy bread and prophecie there.
7.13: But prophecie no more at Beth-el: for it is the Kings chapel, and it is the Kings court.
7.14: Then answered Amos, and said to Amaziah, I was no Prophet, neither was I a prophets sonne, but I was an herdman, and a gatherer of wild figs.
7.15: And the Lord took me as I followed the flock, and the Lord said unto me, Go, prophecie unto my people Israel.
7.16: Now therefore hear thou the word of the Lord. Thou sayest, Prophecie not against Israel, and speak nothing against the house of Izhak.
7.17: Therefore thus sayth the Lord, Thy wife shall be an harlot in the citie, and thy sonnes and thy daughters shall fall by the sword, and thy land shall be deuided by line: and thou shalt die in a polluted land, and Israel shall surely go into captiuitie forth of his land.

8.1: Thus hath the Lord God shewed unto me, and behold, a basket of summer fruit.
8.2: And he said, Amos, what seest thou? And I sayd, A basket of sommer fruit. Then sayd the Lord unto me, The end is come upon my people of Israel, I wil pass by them no more.
8.3: And the songs of the Temple shalbe howlings in that day, saith the Lord God: many dead bodies shalbe in every place: they shall cast them forth with silence.
8.4: Hear this, O yee that swallow up the poor, that ye may make the needie of the land to fayle,
8.5: Saying, When will the new moneth bee gone, that we may sell corn? and the Sabbath, that we may set forth wheat, and make the Ephah small, and the shekel great, and falsifie the weights by deceit?
8.6: That we may buy the poor for silver, and the needie for shooes: yea, and sell the refuse of the wheat.
8.7: The Lord hath sworn by the excellencie of Iaakob, Surely I will never forget any of their workes.
8.8: Shall not the land tremble for this, and every one mourn, that dwelleth therein? and it shall rise up wholy as a flood, and it shall bee cast out, and drowned as by the flood of Egypt.
8.9: And in that day, saith the Lord God, I will even cause the sunne to go down at noon: and I will darken the earth in the clear day.
8.10: And I will turn your feastes into mourning, and all your songs into lamentation: and I will bring sackcloth upon all loynes, and baldnes upon every head: and I will make it as the mourning of an onely sonne, and the end thereof as a bitter day.
8.11: Behold, the dayes come, sayeth the Lord God, that I will send a famine in the land, not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but of hearing the word of the Lord.
8.12: And they shall wander from sea to sea, and from the North even unto the East shall they run to and from to seek the word of the Lord, and shall not find it.
8.13: In that day shall the fair virgines and the yong men perish for thirst.
8.14: They that swear by the sinne of Samaria, and that say, Thy God, O Dan, liveth, and the maner of Beer-sheba liveth, even they shall fall, and never rise up again.

9.1: I saw the Lord standing upon the altar, and he sayde, Smite the lintel of the door, that the postes may shake: and cut them in pieces, even the heads of them all, and I will slay the last of them with the sword: he that fleeth of them, shall not flee away: and he that escapeth of them, shall not be delivered.
9.2: Though they digge into the hell, thence shall mine hand take them: though they clime up to heaven, thence will I bring them down.
9.3: And though they hide them selves in the toppe of Carmel, I will search and take them out thence: and though they be hid from my sight in the bottom of the sea, thence will I command the serpent, and he shall bite them.
9.4: And though they goe into captiuitie before their enemies, thence wil I command the sword, and it shall slay them: and I will set mine eyes upon them for evil, and not for good.
9.5: And the Lord God of hosts shall touch the land, and it shall melt away, and al that dwel therein shall mourn, and it shall rise up wholy like a flood, and shall bee drowned as by the flood of Egypt.
9.6: He buildeth his spheres in the heaven, and hath laid the foundation of his globe of elements in the earth: hee calleth the waters of the sea, and powreth them out upon the open earth: the Lord is his Name.
9.7: Are ye not as the Ethiopians unto mee, O children of Israel, sayeth the Lord? have not I brought up Israel out of the land of Egypt? and the Philistims from Caphtor, and Aram from Kir?
9.8: Behold, the eyes of the Lord God are upon the sinful kingdom, and I will destroy it clean out of the earth. Nevertheless I will not utterly destroy the house of Iaakob, saith the Lord.
9.9: For loe, I will command and I will sift the house of Israel among all nations, like as corn is sifted in a sieve: yet shall not the least stone fall upon the earth.
9.10: But all the sinners of my people shall dye by the sword, which say, The evil shall not come, nor hasten for us.
9.11: In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David, that is fallen down, and close up the breaches therof, and I will rayse up his ruines, and I will build it, as in the dayes of old,
9.12: That they may possess the remnant of Edom, and of all the heathen, because my Name is called upon them, sayeth the Lord, that doeth this.
9.13: Behold, the dayes come, saith the Lord, that the plowman shall touch the mower, and the treader of grapes him that soweth seed: and the mountaines shall drop sweet wine, and all the hilles shall melt.
9.14: And I will bring again the captiuitie of my people of Israel: and they shall build the waste cities, and inhabit the, and they shall plant vineyardes, and drink the wine thereof: they shall also make gardens, and eat the fruites of them.
9.15: And I wil plant them upon their land, and they shall no more bee pulled up again out of their land, which I have given them, sayeth the Lord thy God.

30:1:1: Which as Josephus writeth, was when Uzziah would have usurped the Priest’s office, and therefore was smitten with the leprosy.
Which was a town five miles from Jerusalem in Judea, but he prophesied in Israel.
In his days the kingdom of Israel did most flourish.
30:1:2: Whatsoever is fruitful and pleasant in Israel, shall shortly perish.
30:1:3: He showeth first that all the people round about should be destroyed for their manifold sins: which are meant by three and four, which make seven, because the Israelites should the more deeply consider God’s judgments toward them.

If the Syrians shall not be spared for committing this cruelty against one city, it is not possible that Israel should escape punishment which hath committed so many and grievous sins against God and man.
30:1:4: The antiquity of their buildings shall not avoid my judgments, read Jer. 49:27.
30:1:5: Tiglath-Pileser led the Assyrians captive, and brought them to Cyrene, which he calleth here Kir.
30:1:6: They joined themselves with the Edomites their enemies, which carried them away captives.
30:1:9: For Esau (of whom came the Edomites) and Jacob were brethren, therefore they ought to have admonished them of their brotherly friendship, and not to have provoked them to hatred.
30:1:11: He was a continual enemy unto him.
30:1:13: He noteth the great cruelty of the Ammonites, that spared not the women, but most tyrannously tormented them, and yet the Ammonites came of Lot, who was of the household of Abraham.
30:2:1: For the Moabites were so cruel against the king of Edom, that they burnt his bones after that he was dead: which declared their barbarous rage, seeing they would revenge themselves of the dead.
30:2:4: Seeing the Gentiles that had not so far knowledge were thus punished, Judah which was so fully instructed of the Lord’s will, might not think to escape.
30:2:6: They esteemed most vile bribes more than men’s lives.
If he spare not Judah unto whom his promises were made, much more he will not spare this degenerate kingdom.
30:2:7: When they have spoiled him and thrown him unto the ground, they gape for his life.
30:2:8: They spoil others and offer thereof unto God, thinking that he will dispense with them, when he is made partaker of their iniquity.
Thinking by these ceremonies, that is, by sacrificing, and being near mine altar, they may excuse all their other wickedness.
30:2:9: The destruction of their enemies and his mercy toward them, should have caused their hearts to melt for love toward him.
30:2:11: Ye contemned my benefits, and abused my graces, and craftily went about to stop the mouths of my Prophets.
30:2:13: You have wearied me with your sins, Isa. 1:14.
30:2:14: None shall be delivered by any means.
30:3:2: I have only chosen you to be mine among all other people, and yet you have forsaken me.
30:3:3: Hereby the Prophet signifieth that he speaketh not of himself, but as God guideth and moveth him, which is called the agreement between God and his Prophets.
30:3:4: Will God threaten by his Prophet, except there be some great occasion?
30:3:5: Can anything come without God’s providence?
Shall his threatenings be in vain?
30:3:6: Shall the Prophets threaten God’s judgments and the people not be afraid?
Doth any adversity come without God’s appointment? Isa. 45:7.
30:3:7: God dealeth not with the Israelites, as he doeth with other people: for he ever warneth them before of his plagues by his Prophets.
30:3:8: Because the people ever murmured against the Prophets, he showeth that God’s Spirit moved them so to speak as they did.
30:3:9: He calleth the strangers, as the Philistines and Egyptians, to be witness of God’s judgments against the Israelites for their cruelty and oppression.
30:3:10: The fruit of their cruelty and theft appeareth by their great riches, which they have in their houses.
30:3:12: Where they thought to have had a sure hold, and to have been in safety.
When the lion hath satiate his hunger, the shepherd findeth a leg or a rip of an ear, to show that the sheep have been worried.
30:4:1: They encourage such as have authority over the people to powle them, so that they may have profit by it.
Thus he calleth the princes and governors, which being overwhelmed with the great abundance of God’s benefits, forgot God, and therefore he calleth them by the name of beasts and not of men.
30:4:2: He alludeth to fishers, which catch fish by hooks and thorns.
30:4:4: He speaketh this in contempt of them which resorted to those places, thinking that their great devotion and good intention had been sufficient to have bound God unto them.
30:4:5: You only delight in these outward ceremonies and have none other respect.
30:4:6: That is, lack of bread and meat.
30:4:7: I stayed the rain till the fruits of the earth were destroyed with drought, and yet you would not consider it to return to me by repentance.
30:4:8: They could not find water enough where they had heard say it had rained.
30:4:10: As I plagued the Egyptians, Exod. 9:10.
30:4:11: You were almost all consumed, and a few of you wonderfully preserved, 2 Kings 14:26.
30:5:2: He so calleth them, because they so boasted of themselves or because they were given to wantonness and daintiness.
30:5:3: Meaning, that the tenth part should scarcely be saved.
30:5:5: In those places they worshipped new idols, which aforetime served for the true honor of God: therefore he saith that these shall not save them.
30:5:7: Instead of judgment and equity they execute cruelty and oppression.
30:5:8: He describeth the power of God, Job 9:9.
30:5:10: They hate the Prophets, which reprove them in the open assemblies.
30:5:11: Ye take both his money and also his food, wherewith he should live.
30:5:13: God will so plague them that they shall not suffer the godly once to open their mouths to admonish them of their faults.
30:5:16: So that all degrees shall have matter of lamentation for the great plagues.
30:5:18: Thus he speaketh, because the wicked and hypocrites said they were content to abide God’s judgments, whereas the godly tremble and fear, Jer. 30:7; Joel 2:2, 11; Zeph. 1:15.
30:5:22: Because ye have corrupted my true service, and remain obstinate in your vices, Isa. 1:11; Jer. 6:10.
30:5:24: Do your duty to God, and to your neighbor, and so ye shall feel his grace plentifully, if you show your abundant affections according to God’s word.
30:5:26: That idol which you esteemed as your king, and carried about as you did Chiun, in which images you thought that there was a certain divinity.
30:6:1: These two cities were famous by their first inhabitants the Canaanites: and seeing beforetime they did nothing avail them that were there born, why should you look that they should save you which were brought in to dwell in other men’s possessions?
The Prophet threateneth the wealthy, which regarded not God’s plagues nor menaces by his Prophets.
30:6:2: If God have destroyed these excellent cities in three divers kingdoms, as in Babylon, Syria, and of the Philistines, and hath brought their wide borders into a greater straightness than yours yet are, think you to be better, or to escape?
30:6:3: Ye that continue still in your wickedness, and think that God’s plagues are not at hand, but give yourselves to all idleness, wantonness, and riot.
30:6:5: As he caused divers kinds of instruments to be made to serve God’s glory, so these did contend to invent as many to serve their wanton affections and lusts.
30:6:6: They pitied not their brethren, whereof now many were slain and carried away captive.
30:6:7: Some read, the joy of them that stretch themselves, shall depart.
30:6:8: That is, the riches and pomp.
30:6:10: That is, to some neighbor that dwelleth round about.
The destruction shall be so great, that none shall almost be left to bury the dead: and therefore they shall burn them at home, to carry out the burnt ashes with more ease.

They shall be so astonished at this destruction, that they shall boast no more of the Name of God, and that they are his people: but they shall be dumb when they hear God’s Name, and abhor it, as they that are desperate, or reprobate.
30:6:12: He compareth them to barren rocks, whereupon it is in vain to bestow labor: showing that God’s benefits can have no place among them.
30:6:14: From one corner of the country to another.
30:7:1: After the public commandment for mowing was given: or as some read, when the king’s sheep were shorn.
To devour the land: and he alludeth to the invading of the enemies.
30:7:3: That is, stayed this plague at my prayer.
30:7:4: Meaning, that God’s indignation was inflamed against the stubbornness of this people.
30:7:7: Signifying that this should be the last measuring of the people, and that he would defer his judgment no longer.
30:7:10: That is, when Amos had prophesied that the king should be destroyed: for the wicked Priest more for hatred he bare to the Prophet than for love toward the king, thought this accusation sufficient to condemn him, whereas none other could take place.
30:7:12: When this instrument of Satan was not able to compass his purpose by the king, he assayed by another practice, that was, to fear the Prophet, that he might depart, and not reprove their idolatry there openly, and so hinder his profit.
30:7:14: Thus he showeth by his extraordinary vocation, that God had given him a charge, which he must needs execute.
30:7:17: Thus God used to approve the authority of his Prophets, by his plagues and judgments against them which were malicious enemies, Jer. 28:12 and 29:21, 25, as this day he doeth against them that persecute the ministers of his Gospel.
30:8:2: Which signified the ripeness of their sins, and the readiness of God’s judgments.
30:8:3: There shall be none left to mourn for them.
30:8:4: By staying the sale of food, and necessary things which you have gotten into your own hands, and so cause the poor to spend quickly that little that they have, and at length for necessity to become your slaves.
30:8:5: That is, the measure small, and the price great.
When the dearth was once come they were so greedy of gain, that they thought the holy day to be an hindrance unto them.
30:8:8: That is, the inhabitants of the land shall be drowned, as Nile drowneth many when it overfloweth.
30:8:9: In the midst of their prosperity, I will send great affliction.
30:8:12: Whereby he showeth that they shall not only perish in body, but also in soul for lack of God’s word, which is the food thereof.
30:8:14: For the idolaters did use to swear by their idols: which here he calleth their sin, as the Papists yet do by theirs.
That is, the common manner of worshipping, and the service or religion there used.
30:9:1: Which was at Jerusalem: for he appeared not in the idolatrous places of Israel.
Both the chief of them and also the common people.
30:9:3: He showeth that God will declare himself enemy unto them in all places, and that his elements and all creatures shall be enemies to destroy them.
30:9:6: He declareth by the wonderful power of God, by the making of the heavens and the elements, that it is not possible for man to escape his judgments when he punisheth.
30:9:7: Am I more bound to you than to the Ethiopians, or black moors? yet have I bestowed upon you greater benefits.
30:9:8: Though he destroy the rebellious multitude, yet he will ever reserve the remnant his Church to call upon his Name.
30:9:9: Meaning, that none of his should perish in his wrath.
30:9:11: I will send the Messiah promised, and restore by him the spiritual Israel, Acts 15:16.
30:9:12: Meaning, that the very enemies as were the Edomites, and others should be joined with the Jews in one society, and body, whereof Christ should be the head.
30:9:13: Signifying, that there shall be great plenty of all things, so that when one kind of fruit is ripe, another should follow, and every one in course, Lev. 26:5.
30:9:14: The accomplishment thereof is under Christ, when they are planted in this Church, out of the which they can never be pulled, after they are once grafted therein.
